window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The team maintained a disciplined defensive shape throughout, though there were no immediate turnovers in the opponent's half to test the 6-second press.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The ball carrier consistently maintained at least two passing options, demonstrating excellent positional awareness and support structures.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: Width was successfully maintained across the entire 5-second window, effectively stretching the opponent's defensive block.
window_reviews.highlight: The team demonstrated high-level tactical patience at t=1.0 by utilizing wide channels to stretch the defensive block while maintaining compact internal triangles.
window_reviews.notes: The team is adhering strictly to the positional play philosophy, prioritizing structure and ball retention over risky vertical play.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The red team maintained possession throughout this window, meaning the 6-second rule was not triggered.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The team successfully maintained the required two supporting passing options for the ball carrier throughout the entire 5-second interval.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: The red team consistently maintained wide positioning, effectively stretching the opponent's defensive structure as per the tactical plan.
window_reviews.highlight: The consistent maintenance of wide width and triangular support structures during the midfield build-up at 7.0s facilitated safe ball progression.
window_reviews.notes: The team demonstrates good positional discipline in possession, but the defensive structure remained 'loose' instead of compact, which could be exploited during transitions.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The team failed to demonstrate the high-intensity pressing required during the Red team's buildup, showing a lack of urgency to win the ball back immediately.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The team consistently maintained the required two supporting passing options for the ball carrier throughout the possession phase.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: The team successfully maintained consistent width on the flanks, effectively stretching the opponent's defensive structure during build-up play.
window_reviews.highlight: The transition at 13.0s highlighted a failure in the high-press, as the White team failed to capitalize on the Red team's build-up from the back.
window_reviews.notes: While the team is excellent at maintaining positional structure and passing triangles in possession, the defensive off-the-ball work lacks the required intensity to match the high-pressing philosophy.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The Red team demonstrated effective pressing intensity between 16.0s and 17.0s, successfully challenging the opponent immediately after a loss of possession.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The team largely maintained the required two supporting options for the ball carrier, with only a minor temporary lapse at 17.0s.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: The team consistently maintained width across the entire 5-second window, effectively stretching the opponent's defensive block.
window_reviews.highlight: The Red team successfully regained possession at 19.0s and immediately transitioned back into a structured positional buildup.
window_reviews.notes: The team shows high tactical discipline, particularly in maintaining compact defensive structures and rapid recovery of possession. The momentary drop in supporting options at 17.0s should be addressed to ensure constant passing outlets.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The team failed to demonstrate the high-intensity pressing required by the 6-second rule following the turnover at t=21.0.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The team generally maintained effective support structures in possession, consistently providing the ball carrier with at least two passing options.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: Width was consistently maintained throughout the possession phases, successfully stretching the opponent's defensive block.
window_reviews.highlight: The Red team successfully utilized wide positioning at t=24.0 to initiate a structured transition into the attacking third.
window_reviews.notes: While in-possession structure and width are meeting tactical goals, the team displayed a lack of urgency in defensive transitions, specifically failing to trigger the immediate high press after losing possession.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The team failed to apply the immediate 6-second press upon losing possession at t=26.0, opting for a defensive recovery instead.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The team consistently provided at least two passing options throughout the sequence, adhering well to the positional structure requirements.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: Width was consistently maintained across all frames, successfully stretching the opponent's defensive block during build-up play.
window_reviews.highlight: At t=26.0, the failure to initiate an immediate high press allowed the opponent to transition comfortably into a settled middle-third possession.
window_reviews.notes: While the in-possession positional play is disciplined and compliant with the philosophy, the defensive transition phase is passive and lacks the intensity required by the high-press game plan.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The team failed to demonstrate immediate high-intensity pressing upon the turnover at 32.0s, favoring a delayed structure instead of the required aggressive trap.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The team consistently maintained at least two supporting passing options for the ball carrier, adhering well to the positional play guidelines.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: Width was consistently maintained across the window, effectively stretching the opponent's defensive block to create space in the central channels.
window_reviews.highlight: The Red team successfully utilized wide positioning and consistent supporting structures to maintain possession and progress the ball through the midfield despite defensive pressure.
window_reviews.notes: While the in-possession positional play is excellent and adheres strictly to the Guardiola-influenced structure, the transition to defense remains too passive; the coaching staff needs to enforce the '6-second rule' more aggressively to regain possession quickly.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The team failed to initiate an immediate press upon loss of possession, opting for delayed reactions instead of the mandated high-intensity pressure.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The team maintained supporting options for most of the window, though dropped to a single option during a critical dribble at t=38.0s.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: The team effectively maintained width throughout the window to stretch the opponent's defensive structure.
window_reviews.highlight: The failure to apply high-intensity pressure during the transition at t=37.0s allowed the opponent to progress the ball through the midfield unchallenged.
window_reviews.notes: The defensive line is too passive out of possession; the transition from a compact structure to a high press is non-existent, violating the core pressing philosophy.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The team failed to demonstrate the aggressive high press required by the 6-second rule, showing inconsistency in transition intensity.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The team maintained excellent structural discipline with at least two supporting passing options for the ball carrier throughout the possession phases.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: Width was consistently maintained during attacking phases, effectively stretching the opponent's defensive block.
window_reviews.highlight: The most significant tactical moment was the successful maintenance of passing triangles during the blue team's buildup in the attacking third, providing consistent outlets under pressure.
window_reviews.notes: While the in-possession positional play is well-drilled and structured, the out-of-possession defensive intensity must increase to align with the high-press philosophy; the team was too passive when transitioning to defense.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The team failed to apply any pressure immediately following the transition at 48.0s, completely neglecting the 6-second rule.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: Support structure was inconsistent, falling below the required minimum of two options in frames 46.0s and 47.0s.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: The team successfully maintained tactical width throughout the window, keeping the pitch stretched despite the lack of attacking penetration.
window_reviews.highlight: The transition at 48.0s revealed a significant tactical lapse as the team retreated into a block rather than engaging in the required high press.
window_reviews.notes: The team is prioritizing defensive stability over the high-pressing philosophy requested; the lack of intensity during the turnover phase allowed the opponent to settle in the middle third too easily.

window_reviews.conformance_6_second_rule: The lack of pressing intensity from the defensive unit suggests a failure to apply the 6-second rule when out of possession.
window_reviews.conformance_supporting_triangles: The team consistently maintained at least two supporting passing options, adhering well to the positional structure guidelines.
window_reviews.wing_width_analysis: The team successfully maintained width on the wings, stretching the opponent's defensive block throughout the build-up phase.
window_reviews.highlight: The transition phase at 52.0s demonstrated disciplined off-ball movement, although it lacked the required aggressive defensive pressure.
window_reviews.notes: While the in-possession structure is excellent and follows the Tik-Taka blueprint, the out-of-possession phase is too passive, violating the high-pressing philosophy requested by the coach.
